statement: Do not prescribe fixed proportions of cognitive, affective, and psychomotor outcomes; include each domain only where it is relevant to the programme or course.
condition: when using taxonomies as prompts for outcome design
exception: all three domains may be relevant somewhere across a broad programme

statement: Begin course outcome design with the course's role in the programme, then select important topics and state what students will do with them.
condition: when moving from curriculum aims to course ILOs

statement: Group multiple related topics under outcomes that express a common performance rather than writing several outcomes for every topic.
condition: when a topic-based inventory would create an unmanageable number of outcomes
exception: do not combine topics whose required performances or standards are materially different

statement: Identify the threshold and core concepts among selected topics, then decide which need only declarative treatment and which require functioning use.
condition: when prioritizing content within course outcomes

statement: State explicitly why declarative knowledge is included—general education, enabling background, professional context, or direct support for functioning decisions—because each purpose warrants different depth.
condition: when deciding the role of content knowledge in a course

statement: Prioritize topics at different depths rather than covering every item equally; a curriculum should have deliberate peaks and valleys of emphasis.
condition: when content exceeds what students can learn deeply in available time

statement: Negotiate pressure from multiple teachers or external validators by protecting depth on the programme's most important outcomes rather than allowing every stakeholder topic equal weight.
condition: when shared ownership creates content accretion and over-teaching
exception: mandatory accreditation content still needs to be met, but can be integrated and prioritized

statement: Recognize a breadth-depth trade-off: wider coverage tends toward disconnected acquaintance, while fewer topics permit relational and transferable understanding.
condition: under finite teaching and learning time
exception: better teaching can improve the trade-off but cannot remove all capacity limits

statement: Check whether shallow assessment is masking an overloaded curriculum by allowing acquaintance-level performance to appear adequate.
condition: when extensive content seems to be covered successfully

statement: Calibrate the intended level of understanding to the course stage, discipline, and the programme needs of the learners rather than using one level for every cohort sharing a subject.
condition: when writing outcomes for introductory, advanced, or cross-programme courses
exception: common essential standards may still apply where the same qualification requirement is intended

statement: Determine why a topic is taught—orientation, future background, current state of knowledge, or near-term decision support—before choosing its kind and level of outcome.
condition: when prioritizing topic outcomes

statement: Signal a topic's importance through the depth and type of performance required, not merely through the amount of class time allocated.
condition: when distinguishing priority topics from acquaintance-level topics

statement: Interpret an outcome verb together with its object, originality, context, and required working, because the same verb can represent different structural levels.
condition: when writing or assessing potentially ambiguous verbs such as solve or paraphrase

statement: Use SOLO to reason about structural progression and use other taxonomies as supplementary verb sources rather than assuming every taxonomy category defines a single consistent level.
condition: when selecting verbs for intended outcomes
exception: discipline-specific interpretations still need expert validation

statement: Specify a course outcome through an action verb at the intended level, the content that is its object, and the disciplinary or practical context in which it will be enacted.
condition: when writing an assessable course ILO

statement: Let the selected performance verb imply whether the outcome is primarily declarative or functioning knowledge rather than adding the knowledge label to the student-facing statement.
condition: when the verb and context make the knowledge type clear
exception: design documentation may still record the knowledge type for curriculum analysis

statement: Integrate several topics under one outcome when they share the intended performance, or allow learners to select a suitable topic to demonstrate a common capability.
condition: when keeping the outcome set manageable without losing core course purposes
exception: selection must still yield comparable evidence against the same standard

statement: Remove a lower-level verb from an outcome when a higher-level verb necessarily subsumes it and no distinct evidence is required.
condition: when editing redundant combinations such as describe and explain
exception: retain both only if the course genuinely assesses distinct performances or contexts

statement: Review a course outcome set for relevance to the course aim, coverage of the main reasons for teaching, clarity of level and context, and manageability for alignment.
condition: after drafting course ILOs

statement: Use curriculum mapping to check graduate outcomes against programme outcomes and programme outcomes against the collective course outcomes.
condition: when verifying multilevel curriculum alignment

statement: Use outcome maps to ensure that the relationship between programme outcomes and graduate outcomes was deliberately considered, not to force every programme to address every institutional outcome equally.
condition: when different disciplines have different educational purposes
exception: mandatory institutional policy may constrain the mapping, but relevance should still be made explicit

statement: Check that the complete set of courses addresses every programme outcome and that important outcomes are neither omitted nor disproportionately overemphasized.
condition: when a programme coordinator reviews course-to-programme alignment

statement: Map an outcome across courses at intentionally increasing complexity rather than repeating the same issue at the same level.
condition: when several courses contribute to one programme outcome
exception: deliberate reinforcement at the same level may be warranted if it serves a documented learning need

statement: Use programme mapping to detect both needless duplication and content or capability gaps before students or external stakeholders encounter them.
condition: when reviewing programme coherence

statement: After multilevel mapping, align course learning activities and assessment tasks directly to the course outcomes because that is where the curriculum is enacted.
condition: when completing a constructively aligned curriculum design

statement: In a course outcome containing explain, give every student repeated opportunities to construct and communicate relationships among the relevant components before assessment.
condition: when explanation is an intended learning performance

statement: A conventional lecture is misaligned with an explanation outcome when the teacher performs all the explaining and students mainly listen and record information.
condition: when students receive no systematic opportunity to explain during learning
exception: a lecture can contain aligned activities that require students to explain

statement: Distinguish explaining from describing: explanation requires showing relationships among components, whereas description may only identify or outline them.
condition: when calibrating declarative outcome levels
exception: disciplinary conventions may require more precise definitions of each performance

statement: Use peer explanation, paired talk, or small buzz groups inside a large class to make the students enact an explanation outcome.
condition: when class size constrains individual teacher-student dialogue
exception: provide a way to check and correct the quality of peer explanations

statement: Design reception-learning activities that require learners to organize declarative content into meaningful relationships instead of leaving that structuring work implicit.
condition: when an intended outcome requires a well-structured declarative knowledge base

statement: Treat lectures, tutorials, laboratories, and excursions as settings for learning, then insert specific student activities that enact the intended outcome within each setting.
condition: when selecting a broad teaching format

statement: Select and exercise the learner activity most suited to each intended outcome rather than applying one teaching method to the entire outcome set.
condition: when a course has outcomes requiring different kinds of performance

statement: Do not infer teaching quality from an engaging presentation alone, because presentation ratings can remain high even when the presenter lacks substantive expertise.
condition: when evaluating a lecture or one-off presentation
exception: engagement can still support learning when the content and activities are sound

statement: Use lectures selectively for information delivery, recognizing that independent reading may transmit information more effectively and that lectures are weak vehicles for higher-order thinking.
condition: when deciding whether a lecture is aligned with the intended learning performance
exception: a lecture can incorporate aligned active tasks that require higher-order thinking

statement: Do not rely on lecturing alone to improve attitudes or inspire learners, since such effects are inconsistent and depend heavily on presentation quality.
condition: when motivation or attitude change is an intended outcome
exception: an unusually skilled presenter may motivate some learners

statement: Interrupt extended teacher talk with a pause or a different learner activity roughly every 15 to 20 minutes, while adapting the interval to attention, difficulty, pace, and context.
condition: when students are engaged in sustained, low-variation listening
exception: continue longer only when there is credible evidence that attention remains high

statement: End a prolonged learning period with learner-generated consolidation, because active review improves retention more than simply ending the session.
condition: after an extended presentation or learning sequence

statement: Have students articulate their own understanding to the teacher or a peer during review rather than substituting a teacher-delivered recap for learner activity.
condition: when consolidating material during or at the end of class

statement: Reserve in-person exposition for current disciplinary developments, contested perspectives, and demonstrations of scholarly reasoning that static resources do not provide as well.
condition: when deciding what distinctive value a live lecture should add
exception: teachers without current expertise should use other aligned approaches rather than merely relay readable content

statement: Frame a large scheduled class as a plenary learning session and organize it around student performances aligned to outcomes, not around uninterrupted teacher performance.
condition: when one teacher must work with many students in a lecture theatre

statement: Use required pre-class reading plus short diagnostic responses to expose confusion before class and allocate class time to application and clarification.
condition: when students can acquire foundational information independently before class
exception: access needs or workload constraints may require supported in-class preparation

statement: Interleave conceptual questions with individual responses, peer discussion across differing answers, and a second response so learners must explain and reconsider their reasoning.
condition: when a class is developing conceptual understanding that can be probed with discriminating questions

statement: Combine active work on novel problems with timely feedback from both the instructor and peers when the outcome requires high-level understanding.
condition: when designing interactive teaching for conceptual application

statement: Structure a course-preparation assignment with an explicit outcome, necessary background, and a written task that makes students think with the assigned reading before class.
condition: when replacing information-heavy class time with preparation and discussion

statement: Use small groups to synthesize individual preparation into a shared response, then connect group contributions in a whole-class representation that can seed subsequent work.
condition: when students arrive with completed course-preparation assignments

statement: Treat low-stakes preparation as a learning activity by checking genuine completion and requiring incomplete work to be repeated rather than grading its quality summatively.
condition: when the purpose is to secure preparation for class rather than certify mastery
exception: a different assessment design is needed when the preparation itself is an assessed outcome

statement: Do not assume discussion-intensive course-preparation assignments scale unchanged to very large classes.
condition: when class size substantially exceeds roughly 80 students
exception: redesign with additional facilitation or technology may alter the constraint

statement: Use concept maps when outcomes require learners to integrate ideas, perceive relationships, organize a whole, or expose their current conceptual structure.
condition: when relational organization is central to learning or assessment

statement: Have learners arrange concepts around a core idea and label the relationships they perceive, so the map records both structure and the meaning of its links.
condition: when constructing a concept-map activity

statement: Evaluate a concept map holistically through the sophistication of its organization and the correctness of its relationships rather than by mechanically counting isolated elements.
condition: when a concept map represents a complex conceptual whole

statement: Align teaching and assessment cues with relational learning if students are expected to adopt tools such as concept mapping; perceived irrelevance will otherwise discourage use.
condition: when introducing a learning strategy that competes with memorization

statement: Establish learning partners or small stable groups as a support structure for clarification, peer explanation, and aligned collaborative tasks in large classes.
condition: when learners benefit from routine access to a peer
exception: respect a learner's informed preference to work independently

statement: Permit unsuccessful learning partnerships to be re-formed rather than treating the original match as fixed.
condition: when interpersonal compatibility prevents the partnership from supporting learning

statement: Use very short written prompts at the start and end of class to elicit preparation goals, perceived main learning, and unresolved questions, then feed the responses into the next teaching decision.
condition: when rapid formative evidence is needed from a large group

statement: Separate listening time from recording time and have students compare and revise notes if note taking is intended to develop understanding.
condition: when note taking is used as a learning activity during a presentation
exception: provide source materials directly when the only goal is an accurate record for later use

statement: Teach note-taking strategies within the disciplinary content and purpose they are meant to serve rather than as decontextualized study skills.
condition: when note taking supports a specific content area or intended outcome

statement: Model expert problem solving or composing by making decisions, revisions, and mistakes visible, then require students to perform the process themselves.
condition: when learners need access to an otherwise hidden expert process
exception: observation alone is insufficient when active performance is the outcome

statement: Embed short work-along exercises in an exposition so students immediately apply each concept and make their reasoning visible.
condition: when teaching procedural or applied concepts to a large class

statement: Provide accurate skeleton notes or diagrams with space for learners to identify main ideas, paraphrase them, and add examples rather than making transcription the central task.
condition: when presentation materials contain structures or diagrams students need to retain

statement: Use peer teaching as a core learning resource in large classes because explaining content can deepen both tutor and tutee learning, often benefiting the tutor most.
condition: when course outcomes can be enacted through explanation, questioning, or guided practice
exception: peer teaching requires design and preparation rather than simply delegating instruction

statement: Have peer tutors reason from the learner's less-developed perspective, take responsibility for accuracy, and revisit how they themselves learned the topic.
condition: when designing the tutor role to produce learning for the tutor

statement: Expect student-led groups to explore a wider range of ideas and sometimes produce more complex outcomes than teacher-led groups.
condition: when peer groups are adequately prepared and the task supports discussion

statement: Specify a peer-mentoring programme's intended outcomes, context, interaction model, and participant roles before implementation.
condition: when creating academic mentoring or peer-tutoring provision

statement: Prepare peer tutors to explain, question, monitor comprehension, connect new and prior knowledge, and construct understanding rather than merely transmit content.
condition: when peer tutors are expected to gain cognitively from teaching

statement: Select cross-year study-session leaders for both strong prior performance and suitable interpersonal qualities, then train them to model, advise, and facilitate rather than replace the curriculum teacher.
condition: when operating a PASS-style programme

statement: Support peer leaders with initial training, continuing coordinator meetings, direct awareness of the taught course, and reflective records that feed current problems back to staff.
condition: when maintaining a structured peer-assisted study programme

statement: Use ongoing peer-leader feedback to diagnose teaching problems during the course rather than depending solely on end-of-course evaluations.
condition: when peer leaders have regular contact with participating students

statement: Keep PASS-style attendance voluntary and let students set a review-oriented agenda without introducing new course material.
condition: when the programme supplements rather than replaces the formal course
exception: local programme requirements may justify a different participation model if its purpose is explicit

statement: Prioritize peer-assisted study support for large, technically demanding, high-failure, internationally diverse, or multi-programme service courses.
condition: when limited peer-support resources must be allocated

statement: Keep students engaged in activities relevant to the intended outcomes and provide recurring instructor, peer, and self-assessment feedback in large classes.
condition: when converting a lecture theatre into an effective learning environment

statement: Reassess the purpose and structure of tutorials when interactive plenary teaching already performs their intended elaboration and clarification functions.
condition: when tutorial groups are too large, weakly staffed, or duplicate aligned work done elsewhere
exception: retain a tutorial when it provides a distinct, well-designed learning function

statement: For student-led tutorials, pre-check brief student presentations, assign discussion questions, require each learner to surface a point of confusion, and reserve instructor time for unresolved issues.
condition: when redesigning a tutorial around learner ownership

statement: Use spontaneous student questions and comments to reconstruct ideas collaboratively, while keeping attention on the learners' reasoning rather than the instructor's improvisational performance.
condition: when a smaller class permits responsive interaction

statement: Interpret a student's question through the conceptual perspective that produced it and connect that partial understanding to the expert structure of the topic.
condition: when responding to student questions about difficult or threshold concepts

statement: Use convergent questioning to guide a class toward a warranted shared structure; a question with a target answer need not be cognitively low-level.
condition: when the learning goal has a defensible answer or conceptual structure
exception: do not present a genuinely contested issue as if only one answer were possible

statement: Use divergent questions to draw on learner experience, generate interpretations, support reflection, and connect practical knowledge to conceptual frameworks.
condition: when multiple defensible responses can advance the outcome
exception: provide direction when open discussion becomes unrelated or aimless

statement: Allow substantially more silent thinking time for reflective, hypothetical, or open-ended questions than for factual recall, because response quality tends to improve with adequate wait time.
condition: when asking high-level or divergent questions

statement: Use asynchronous discussion when higher-level responses require more thinking time than a live class can comfortably provide.
condition: when delayed response can improve the depth of learners' reasoning
exception: immediate interaction may still be needed for time-critical feedback or collaborative momentum

statement: Audit a class by listing its intended outcomes, the activities that occurred, and who actually performed each activity; redesign where the learners were not doing the work required by the outcomes.
condition: when reviewing or redesigning a large-class session

statement: Prepare large-class procedures more explicitly than small-class procedures because transitions, improvisation, and recovery become slower and riskier as enrolment grows.
condition: when managing a large plenary session

statement: Establish signals, question procedures, peer-group arrangements, reporting roles, and transition rules during the first large-class session.
condition: when recurring student interaction must be coordinated at scale

statement: At the start of a large session, signal a clear beginning, show the structure and sequence, connect to prior work, and state what the live session adds beyond available texts.
condition: when orienting a large group to a plenary learning sequence

statement: When course information is already available online, use live time for aligned activity and require purposeful preparation if that information is prerequisite.
condition: when learners can access the presentation content at their own pace
exception: live exposition remains justified when it adds current expertise, perspective, or needed scaffolding

statement: Turn an individual student's spoken question into a whole-class learning event by stepping back, repeating or reframing it audibly, and involving the group in the response.
condition: when handling questions in a large room
exception: use written collection or microphones when speech cannot be heard reliably

statement: Reduce large-class anonymity through visible accessibility, peer introductions, informed use of names and interests, sampling delegated assessment, and dependable contact availability.
condition: when class size risks creating an impersonal or alienating climate
exception: collect and use personal information only with appropriate privacy and cultural care

statement: Use humour, topical references, and colloquial language cautiously in culturally diverse classes because shared context cannot be assumed.
condition: when many learners may not share the instructor's linguistic or cultural references

statement: Preserve constructive alignment in large classes by matching learner activities and assessment tasks to the intended outcome verbs; enrolment size is not a reason to abandon alignment.
condition: when adapting teaching and assessment for scale

statement: Educate professionals to make informed choices grounded in knowledge, not merely to reproduce procedures for which they were trained.
condition: when an outcome concerns professional rather than purely technical performance

statement: Design professional learning to both build an adequate declarative knowledge base and require learners to put that knowledge to work.
condition: when preparing learners for informed professional decisions and performance

statement: Choose deliberately between building knowledge before application and developing knowledge as practice creates a need for it.
condition: when sequencing declarative and functioning knowledge
exception: a programme may combine both sequences for different outcomes

statement: Require students to perform the outcome verb during learning; an instructor discussing or demonstrating application does not give learners practice in applying.
condition: when an intended outcome uses a functioning verb such as apply, design, plan, create, or solve
exception: explanation and modelling may precede, but cannot replace, learner performance

statement: Do not postpone a learner's first attempt at a functioning performance until the final assessment.
condition: when students will be assessed on application or another enacted capability

statement: Design the learning activity and assessment around the same authentic performance named in the outcome whenever feasible.
condition: when an outcome can be enacted as both practice and evidence of achievement
exception: use a different task only when it still elicits the same intended performance validly

statement: Assess creation of a professional capability through its performance, while assessing explanation of that capability through a separate declarative task.
condition: when a course distinguishes doing from explaining why the doing matters

statement: Complete an application outcome by specifying what knowledge or method is applied, to what object or person, and in which context.
condition: when writing an intended outcome with the verb apply

statement: Build cases that address the intended outcomes with adequate complexity, include realistic irrelevant detail, require active engagement, and challenge learners to hypothesize and reflect.
condition: when designing case-based learning to connect theory and practice
exception: complexity and noise should remain proportionate to learner readiness

statement: Progress from analysing completed cases to having learners conduct or manage cases themselves when developing functioning knowledge.
condition: when learners need both interpretive scaffolding and independent performance
exception: ethical, safety, or access constraints may require simulation rather than live cases

statement: Sequence cases across a course so their content and demands collectively build the intended knowledge structure rather than presenting disconnected examples.
condition: when case-based learning carries a substantial portion of the syllabus

statement: Monitor and adjust case-based learning workload because excessive demands can trigger more surface-oriented study even when higher-level outcomes improve.
condition: when introducing or scaling a case-intensive course

statement: Use small-group interaction to expose alternative interpretations, make reasoning processes visible, derive standards for judging interpretations, and apply theory to practice.
condition: when functioning outcomes benefit from comparison and reflection

statement: Ensure every group member has enough relevant knowledge or experience to make an informed contribution before expecting productive discussion.
condition: when assigning collaborative work
exception: a jigsaw design may distribute different prerequisite knowledge deliberately

statement: Create a discussion climate in which learners can test interpretations without the instructor immediately correcting, arbitrating, or reclaiming the expert role.
condition: when the purpose of group work is for students to examine and improve their own reasoning
exception: intervene when safety, ethics, or persistent misinformation requires correction

statement: Choose group size by whether each member can retain responsibility and commitment, not by a universal numerical rule.
condition: when forming groups for a specific task and cohort
exception: culture and group dynamics can change how size affects effort

statement: Nominate each group's spokesperson before work begins so reporting responsibility is clear and individuals can present the group's position rather than defend a personal claim.
condition: when small groups will report to a plenary

statement: Consider random group assignment when self-selected friendship groups repeatedly drift off task.
condition: when voluntary grouping produces persistent social rather than academic interaction
exception: deliberate matching may be preferable when task roles or accessibility needs require it

statement: Give buzz groups an unambiguous question, problem, or application task; use freer brainstorming only when generation, speculation, or hypothesizing is the intended performance.
condition: when inserting brief group discussion into a class

statement: Use jigsaw groups to distribute active responsibility for a complex task, then require each learner to integrate and reflect on the complete solution.
condition: when a task can be divided into interdependent subproblems
exception: do not assess only a learner's subtask when the outcome concerns understanding the whole

statement: Use pairs for joint work on a problem or skill in laboratories, at computer workstations, or on structured question-and-answer tasks.
condition: when close reciprocal participation is more useful than a larger group

statement: Give judgement-learning groups ambiguous evidence that supports competing hypotheses, then require learners to compare the evidence and theories behind their differing conclusions.
condition: when professional judgement must remain open to alternative interpretations
exception: the ambiguity must not conceal a safety-critical standard that learners are required to follow

statement: Design syndicate tasks to draw on both selected sources and learners' direct experience, then consolidate the groups' emerging conceptual structures in a teacher-led plenary.
condition: when intensive small-group debate should feed a shared course structure

statement: Include higher-level group performances in assessment if the course expects group work to develop those performances.
condition: when collaboration is intended to enhance analysis, application, or other high-level skills

statement: Match group modality to the interaction needed: use asynchronous exchange for considered individual contributions and face-to-face exchange for rapid spontaneous discussion.
condition: when choosing between online and in-person group work
exception: hybrid sequences can use different modes for different phases

statement: Train students to ask each other relational prompts about main ideas, distinctions, comparisons, examples, and implications when the goal is high-level elaboration.
condition: when peer interaction must produce critical thinking rather than unstructured talk

statement: Give student interaction a clear, cognitively demanding agenda; longer open discussion does not by itself produce higher-level thought.
condition: when collaborative activity targets a specific high-level outcome
exception: open exploration may be appropriate when generating possibilities is itself the outcome

statement: Permit and clarify legitimate peer collaboration during planning and resource discovery while preserving individual responsibility for work that must demonstrate individual achievement.
condition: when students spontaneously collaborate on an individually assessed assignment
exception: collaboration boundaries must follow the stated assessment-integrity rules

statement: Define workplace-learning outcomes around integrating university knowledge with practice, applying theory and skills, collaborating across roles, and acting with professional and ethical responsibility.
condition: when designing a placement, practicum, clinical, attachment, or internship experience
exception: discipline-specific outcomes should extend this common core

statement: Require placement educators to coordinate logistics, select suitable cases or projects, design activities, scaffold performance, provide feedback, and assess the intended outcomes.
condition: when a workplace supervisor carries teaching responsibility

statement: Organize workplace learning around a cycle of gathering evidence, identifying the problem, applying theory to formulate a response, acting, evaluating effects, improving, collaborating, and reflecting.
condition: when the professional context permits learners to participate in a complete practice cycle
exception: scope and supervision must reflect learner readiness and professional safety

statement: Integrate placement and classroom learning through explicit shared outcomes, a visible theory-practice connection, and structured reflection on experience.
condition: when learners move between structured institutional learning and less-structured workplace participation

statement: Secure close institution-workplace agreement on learning opportunities, outcome meanings, and performance rubrics because supervisors and academic staff may value different things.
condition: when workplace personnel supervise or assess students
exception: differences that reflect legitimate workplace requirements should be reconciled rather than suppressed

statement: Use a negotiated learning contract to involve a student and placement educator in specifying learning needs, activities, and assessment within the authentic context.
condition: when a placement permits individualization of the learning experience
exception: non-negotiable professional, legal, or safety standards still apply

statement: Teach creativity as the generation and evaluation of new ideas and teach innovation as carrying worthwhile novelty into effective implementation.
condition: when defining creative outcomes across professional or academic fields

statement: Treat convergent and divergent thinking as complementary processes in advanced work rather than as fixed learner abilities or mutually exclusive modes.
condition: when designing or evaluating high-level thinking

statement: Build sufficient disciplinary knowledge before expecting informed generation, theorizing, or reflection, while recognizing that knowledge mastery alone does not produce creative use.
condition: when sequencing foundational and creative learning
exception: prior experience may supply the necessary knowledge outside the formal course sequence

statement: Ask learners to create discipline-grounded works or solutions that add something original, rather than treating creativity as an abstract personal trait.
condition: when operationalizing a creativity outcome

statement: Use open-ended outcome verbs such as design, invent, or create to align outcomes-based education with an unscripted creative process rather than a predetermined product.
condition: when the intended outcome is genuinely creative
exception: competency outcomes with one required answer remain appropriately more closed

statement: Trigger a creative outcome through discipline-specific generation activities, individual development, and opportunities for peer feedback rather than prescribing a universal creativity exercise.
condition: when selecting teaching activities for an open-ended creative verb

statement: Connect repeated performance to structured reflection so learners can judge whether their thinking changed the quality of their doing.
condition: when creative practice develops through rehearsal, improvisation, or iteration

statement: Use adaptive or simulation media to let learners vary parameters and receive consequences intrinsic to their actions, thereby supporting exploratory inquiry.
condition: when a digital environment can respond meaningfully to learner choices
exception: external explanation remains necessary when the simulation's feedback is ambiguous or misleading

statement: Create a climate in which learners can risk unusual hypotheses without ridicule from the instructor or peers.
condition: when creative or divergent responses are sought
exception: respectful critique of consequences and evidence is still required

statement: Delay dismissive judgement of an apparently irrelevant response and first invite the learner or class to explain the underlying connection.
condition: when a response may encode a non-obvious analogy or insight
exception: intervene directly when the response harms others or derails the learning environment

statement: Avoid relying on high-anxiety, tightly invigilated conditions to elicit adventurous or original work, because such climates tend to suppress creative responding.
condition: when assessing creativity
exception: controlled conditions may still be required for other validity or integrity purposes, but their effect on creativity must be recognized

statement: Define lifelong learning within a field as the capacity to handle unforeseen disciplinary or professional problems, not as an unbounded promise to handle anything.
condition: when turning lifelong learning into attainable programme outcomes

statement: Prepare learners to identify and acquire knowledge at the point an authentic problem creates a need for it.
condition: when designing for just-in-time or work-based lifelong learning
exception: foundational knowledge that cannot safely be deferred should be established in advance

statement: For emergent problems, establish relationships, resources, and informed conversations that can respond as needs crystallize rather than pretending the full curriculum can be predetermined.
condition: when real work produces unpredictable, highly contextual learning needs
exception: required standards and foundational concepts still need explicit planning

statement: Support lifelong learning externally through aligned workplace activities and assessment, and internally by teaching independent information use, problem solving, reflection, and intellectual autonomy.
condition: when assigning institutional responsibility for graduate lifelong-learning capacity

statement: Teach learners to find new information, judge its importance, use it, and solve novel non-textbook problems against an abstract theoretical base.
condition: when developing information literacy for independent professional learning

statement: Distinguish generic organization skills, content-specific learning strategies, and reflective self-management when planning support for self-directed learning.
condition: when diagnosing which kind of study or learning capability students need

statement: Teach planning, deadline management, systematic record keeping, and strategic searching explicitly when learners lack these generic study-management skills.
condition: when generic organization is constraining academic performance

statement: Do not teach study techniques as context-free recipes when course teaching and assessment signal that factual reproduction is what counts; students may repurpose the techniques for surface memorization.
condition: when introducing reading, note-taking, writing, or examination strategies
exception: generic management skills can still be taught separately when their application is connected back to course demands

statement: Embed strategies for acquiring, working with, and demonstrating information in the specific course content and assessment contexts where students will use them.
condition: when teaching content-related study skills

statement: Develop informed self-direction by combining a sound knowledge base with metacognitive strategies for framing novel problems, testing information, trying solutions, and monitoring improvement.
condition: when preparing learners for fuzzy or emergent problems

statement: Teach divergent generation alongside convergent self-monitoring so learners both produce possible responses and evaluate whether their work remains adequate and on track.
condition: when learners manage open-ended professional problems

statement: Use self-assessment and peer assessment as learning activities that develop professional self-evaluation, not only as mechanisms for assigning marks.
condition: when graduates need to judge and improve their own work
exception: formal certification still requires appropriate independent judgement

statement: Use reflective diaries and critical-incident analysis to make learners diagnose performance and propose better future responses.
condition: when experience-based learning requires structured reflection

statement: Use portfolios to connect evidence and reflection from inside and outside class to a learner's longer-term educational or career goals.
condition: when learners need a structured record of developmental reflection
exception: a portfolio without guided selection and reflection may become only an archive

statement: Align professional education by having learners perform authentic professional problems under appropriate guidance and assess the quality of that same performance.
condition: when safeguards allow realistic enactment of the intended professional outcome
exception: use simulation or staged responsibility where direct practice would be unsafe or unethical

statement: Design problem-based learning to build usable knowledge, professional reasoning, contextual self-direction, motivation, and—where relevant—workplace-like collaboration.
condition: when adopting PBL rather than isolated problem exercises
exception: a programme may weight these goals differently according to its intended outcomes

statement: Adjust problem structure and instructor direction to learner readiness, ranging from fully specified problems with substantial guidance to ill-defined problems requiring independent inquiry.
condition: when calibrating a PBL design
exception: minimal direction should not remove necessary safety, ethical, or access scaffolds

statement: Start PBL with a problem, query, or puzzle that drives learners to seek the disciplines, facts, and procedures they need, rather than teaching the content conventionally before assigning a problem.
condition: when claiming that a course uses problem-based rather than problem-solving learning
exception: brief prerequisite preparation may be necessary when novices cannot enter the problem safely or meaningfully

statement: Select PBL problems for the professional knowledge, contextual skills, self-management, attitudes, and judgement learners will acquire while solving them, not merely for the immediate answer.
condition: when choosing the problem sequence for a course

statement: Construct PBL problems that integrate relevant disciplines, open multiple defensible options, activate prior knowledge, create a need for new knowledge, prompt elaboration and self-direction, and address the course outcomes.
condition: when authoring an open or ill-structured problem
exception: not every problem must carry every programme outcome, but the sequence must cover them deliberately

statement: Map the cross-disciplinary concepts, knowledge, and skills a problem may evoke before writing the intended learner performances and selecting authentic situations that cover them.
condition: when designing a coherent PBL problem set

statement: Present a PBL situation with a concrete context and practitioner role, specific data, and a required deliverable such as a decision or report.
condition: when writing an authentic problem brief
exception: withholding some data is appropriate when finding that information is part of the outcome

statement: Use staged release of new events or data when an authentic problem evolves over time and learners should revise their response as conditions change.
condition: when a roll-out problem better represents professional practice

statement: Provide PBL facilitators with the problem, intended learning issues and outcomes, necessary content background, and suggested learner resources.
condition: when multiple facilitators must support a common problem consistently
exception: the guide should scaffold facilitation without scripting away learner inquiry

statement: Begin a PBL sequence with a consequential authentic context that gives learners an immediate reason to acquire and use knowledge.
condition: when initiating problem-based professional learning
exception: authenticity must remain compatible with novice safety and ethical safeguards

statement: Move learners quickly into small problem-solving groups and interaction with relevant teachers, peers, or clients rather than delaying participation until after extensive exposition.
condition: when the PBL problem can meaningfully activate current knowledge
exception: brief orientation may be needed before learners can participate responsibly

statement: Have PBL learners state what they know, verify it, identify what is missing, seek varied resources, and reconvene to elaborate and consolidate the resulting knowledge around the case.
condition: during a problem inquiry cycle

statement: Make recurring review of the problem, learning process, self-management, and self-monitoring part of PBL rather than focusing only on the proposed solution.
condition: throughout a PBL programme

statement: Require learners to apply acquired knowledge back to the live problem and receive feedback throughout the process.
condition: when knowledge is being developed for functioning use in PBL

statement: Calibrate PBL problem structure and teacher direction to the educational philosophy, departmental aims, learner expectations, and degree of autonomy the cohort can initially manage.
condition: when introducing PBL to a particular programme or learner group
exception: adjust support over time as learners demonstrate greater self-direction

statement: Make PBL assessment expectations explicit for learners whose prior education trained them to infer hidden marking schemes from examinations.
condition: when students are unfamiliar with open, workplace-like learning and assessment
exception: clarity should not reduce an ill-structured problem to a single scripted answer

statement: Expect learners with substantial workplace experience to adapt more readily to PBL when its problem-solving process resembles their work.
condition: when PBL mirrors familiar workplace practice
exception: individual experience and prior educational expectations still vary

statement: Evaluate PBL against its intended clinical or professional performances and learning strategies, not only against basic-science recall examinations.
condition: when comparing PBL with traditional instruction
exception: declarative knowledge that is itself an outcome still requires valid assessment

statement: PBL participants tend to report greater enjoyment, use more self-directed and higher-level learning strategies, and show progressively deeper approaches than traditionally taught peers.
condition: across the studies summarized in the cited review
exception: outcomes depend on implementation quality and the assessment system

statement: PBL graduates generally perform comparably or sometimes better in clinical work while often performing worse on conventional examinations of basic declarative science.
condition: in the medical-education evidence summarized by the source
exception: results should not be generalized unchanged to every discipline or assessment design

statement: Teach novices to reason explicitly from hypotheses and first principles through predicted evidence rather than imitate experts' compressed data-driven recognition.
condition: when learners lack the experience needed for reliable pattern recognition
exception: experienced practitioners can use data-driven recognition for familiar cases but should return to explicit reasoning for unfamiliar or complex cases

statement: Encourage PBL learners to consult multiple appropriate knowledge resources instead of treating a single textbook as the complete basis for judgement.
condition: when investigating a problem whose solution requires new information
exception: sources still require evaluation for relevance and reliability

statement: Include implementation costs, cohort size, self-directed study, and the number and size of facilitated groups when comparing PBL with lecture-based provision.
condition: when assessing the feasibility or cost-benefit of PBL
exception: published cost estimates are context-specific and should not be treated as universal thresholds

statement: Align the interpersonal climate with PBL by having tutors facilitate inquiry rather than use expertise to withhold, dominate, or belittle.
condition: when tutors support learners' questioning and problem solving
exception: facilitators still intervene to maintain safety, ethics, and productive boundaries

statement: Do not retain an assessment that rewards traditional literature reproduction when the outcomes and learning activities emphasize applying knowledge to problems.
condition: when PBL is the intended course design
exception: literature analysis may be assessed separately when it remains an explicit intended outcome

statement: Judge the trade-off between less prescribed content coverage and stronger capacity to identify and fill knowledge gaps at the point of need.
condition: when evaluating a PBL curriculum that covers less of a traditional syllabus
exception: critical foundational knowledge that cannot safely be deferred must remain guaranteed

statement: Keep PBL theory-based so authentic performance is informed by explanatory knowledge rather than reduced to unexamined apprenticeship.
condition: when learners practise professional skills through problems

statement: Prepare teachers in PBL to shift from presenting their specialty as the organizing centre to facilitating integration and application across knowledge areas.
condition: when faculty expertise and identity are organized around separate disciplines
exception: teachers' specialist knowledge remains a resource when offered in response to the problem rather than dominating it

statement: Provide cross-departmental flexibility for PBL because authentic problems commonly require knowledge that does not fit a single departmental boundary.
condition: when institutional structures would otherwise fragment multidisciplinary problem learning
exception: single-discipline problems may not require the same organizational change

statement: Audit functioning-knowledge teaching by identifying the intended verb, the actual teacher and student activities, and who performs that verb; revise any design in which only the teacher enacts it.
condition: when reviewing teaching activities for a practical outcome

statement: Match each group-work form to the specific intended outcome rather than treating collaboration as a generic method.
condition: when choosing among brainstorming, buzz groups, jigsaws, dyads, reciprocal questioning, syndicates, or spontaneous groups

statement: Prepare undergraduates for later just-in-time learning through information literacy, reflective self-direction, strategic search, contextual learning skills, and deliberate improvement from prior practice.
condition: when lifelong learning is a programme aim

statement: Treat PBL outcomes as implementation-sensitive: an expert-dominating climate or misaligned examination can negate the benefits of an otherwise coherent problem design.
condition: when PBL is embedded in conventional teaching and assessment systems

statement: Design assessment tasks as authentic representations of the intended learning outcomes because anticipated assessment strongly directs what and how students learn.
condition: when planning course assessment
exception: unexpected worthwhile outcomes may require additional ways to recognize learning without displacing the intended outcomes

statement: Separate formative assessment for improving ongoing learning and teaching from summative assessment for final grading or accreditation.
condition: when defining the purpose of an assessment event
exception: the same task format may serve both purposes at different, clearly identified times

statement: Use formative evidence to adjust both an individual learner's next action and the teacher's instructional response.
condition: during learning while improvement is still possible

statement: Design teaching activities to expose current performance and provide feedback, because feedback capacity is a central source of a teaching method's effectiveness.
condition: when comparing or selecting teaching methods

statement: Make formative learning safe enough for students to reveal errors and uncertainties, since correction depends on first detecting them.
condition: when an activity is intended to diagnose and improve learning
exception: harmful or integrity-related conduct may still require consequences distinct from misunderstanding

statement: Develop learners' ability to detect and correct their own errors through self-assessment and peer assessment.
condition: when preparing learners to regulate the quality of their own work
exception: novices need criteria, exemplars, and calibration before independent judgements can be trusted

statement: Do not expect candid error disclosure when the same performance immediately determines a consequential grade.
condition: when an assessment event combines formative and summative stakes
exception: low-stakes or recoverable grading designs may reduce, but not eliminate, the conflict

statement: Tell students explicitly which continuous-assessment events are formative and which contribute summatively so they can participate under the correct expectations.
condition: when assessment recurs throughout a course and only some results count toward the final grade

statement: Reuse an aligned performance formatively during practice and summatively at the end only when its changing purpose is unmistakable to learners.
condition: when the same kind of task can validly evidence progress and final achievement

statement: Design assessment on the assumption that students will prioritize what they expect to be tested on and adopt the strategies the task rewards.
condition: when anticipating assessment backwash
exception: individual learners may pursue additional goals, but course design should not depend on that

statement: Embed the intended outcomes directly in assessment tasks so strategic preparation drives the desired learning rather than superficial test tactics.
condition: when using assessment backwash constructively

statement: Avoid examination designs that make mark-maximizing tactics more rewarding than complete, well-reasoned responses.
condition: when time allocation and point schemes encourage learners to start every answer but finish none

statement: Use a standards model rather than a measurement model when the purpose is to judge whether learners achieved specified educational outcomes.
condition: when assessing classroom learning after students have been admitted
exception: measurement and norm comparison may be appropriate for research, diagnosis, or selection among excess qualified applicants

statement: Do not reduce multidimensional understanding to the quantity of correct content when outcomes require integration, critical analysis, hypothesizing, or other qualitative change.
condition: when intended outcomes exceed unistructural or multistructural recall
exception: counts can validly assess a narrowly quantitative outcome

statement: Do not assume equal percentages represent equal standards across different subjects, tasks, cohorts, or course levels.
condition: when comparing or combining percentage scores
exception: a validated common scale with demonstrated equivalence would be needed to justify direct comparison

statement: Do not design attainment assessments to manufacture a bell-shaped spread, because admitted cohorts are not random populations and achievement reflects teaching and learning as well as initial ability.
condition: when assessing achievement in a taught course
exception: a naturally occurring distribution can be reported descriptively without forcing grades to match it

statement: Interpret a concentration of high achievement as potentially consistent with effective teaching rather than as automatic evidence of weak standards.
condition: when many students independently meet predeclared high standards
exception: the assessment and grading judgements still require moderation for validity

statement: Avoid making consequential distinctions at one-mark precision when scoring error and unequal scale intervals make that precision indefensible.
condition: when marks arise from qualitative judgements or small classroom samples
exception: a genuinely calibrated measurement instrument may support finer distinctions

statement: Make pass, fail, and grade-boundary decisions through holistic judgement against public performance criteria rather than by accumulating unexplained micro-marks.
condition: when the performance is qualitatively structured and consequential
exception: component scores may inform the judgement when their criteria and combination are educationally defensible

statement: Use comparison between applicants only to allocate scarce places after checking necessary entry standards, not as the basis for grading learning within the admitted cohort.
condition: when distinguishing selection from educational assessment

statement: Do not cap the proportion of learners receiving a grade when all meet its stated standard.
condition: when grades are meant to report criterion-referenced achievement
exception: competitive awards or selection decisions should be labelled and handled separately

statement: Reject grading on a curve for aligned assessment because it reports relative rank regardless of the actual quality reached and predetermines the distribution.
condition: when the purpose is to certify achievement of intended outcomes
exception: rank information may be reported separately for a legitimate selection purpose

statement: Do not treat all correct items or isolated points as educationally interchangeable merely because they contribute one mark each.
condition: when an outcome depends on particular concepts, structures, or performances
exception: equally weighted items are defensible only when their equivalence is substantively justified

statement: Set a pass standard from the minimum acceptable performance, not by assuming that half of the available marks universally represents competence.
condition: when determining a passing threshold

statement: Assess the organization, concepts, theories, narratives, skills, or performances that constitute learning rather than their arbitrary conversion into a count of points.
condition: when the intended outcome has a meaningful whole or structure
exception: a count remains useful when quantity itself is the intended performance

statement: Plan assessment together with outcomes and teaching activities rather than treating it as a standardized administrative event designed near the end of teaching.
condition: when designing or revising a course

statement: Question standardized, decontextualized assessment conditions when they are imposed primarily to compare students and consequently sample only lower-order outcomes.
condition: when authentic outcomes require tools, context, collaboration, or extended performance
exception: standardized conditions can be appropriate when they are intrinsic to the intended outcome or necessary for a valid decision

statement: Avoid assessment schemes that signal isolated facts matter more than their relationships, because they promote multistructural accumulation over integrated understanding.
condition: when intended outcomes require relational or extended-abstract learning

statement: Use standards that make improvement controllable by learners rather than norm-referenced outcomes that depend on who else happens to be assessed.
condition: when assessment should motivate purposeful learning
exception: competitive selection necessarily adds a relative decision after standards have been considered

statement: Do not let bureaucratic convenience, numerical familiarity, plagiarism control, or tradition substitute for evidence that an assessment validly represents the intended learning.
condition: when defending inherited measurement-model practices
exception: administrative feasibility remains a legitimate constraint after educational validity is secured

statement: Report educational achievement by how well each learner's performance meets predeclared criteria, independently of other learners' results.
condition: when assessing change produced by university learning
exception: relative ranking may be added only for a distinct competitive selection decision

statement: Align an outcome, its learning activity, and its assessment around the same performance: state what learners should do, teach them to do it, and observe whether they can.
condition: when a capability can be demonstrated directly
exception: use a valid proxy only when direct performance is impractical or unsafe

statement: Permit reasonable reassessment and further learning until a preset standard is reached when mastery, rather than one-shot selection, is the purpose.
condition: when the course can support mastery learning and the standard remains constant
exception: attempts may be bounded by time, resources, progression rules, or safety

statement: Define mastery standards qualitatively in terms of performance quality rather than as a quota of correct detail that can reward memorization.
condition: when outcomes concern structured understanding or skilled performance
exception: quantitative criteria remain appropriate for genuinely quantitative outcomes

statement: Translate appropriately written outcomes into ordered performance levels and use explicit task- or outcome-level rubrics to support grade judgements.
condition: when implementing criterion-referenced grading
exception: rubrics should guide informed judgement rather than become point-count checklists

statement: Allow different task formats or working conditions to demonstrate the same standard when learners can reach valid optimal performance in different ways.
condition: when the decision concerns attainment rather than rank under identical conditions
exception: all alternatives must elicit comparable evidence of the same outcome and preserve necessary integrity constraints

statement: Develop assessors' shared understanding of what poor, acceptable, good, and excellent whole performances look like and why.
condition: when teachers must make holistic standards-based judgements

statement: Make outcomes and grade-level criteria visible enough that students can monitor their progress and identify how to improve.
condition: when using standards-based assessment to generate constructive backwash
exception: clarity need not prescribe a single acceptable response to an open outcome

statement: Use authentic outcome-aligned tasks so learners can see the relevance of assessment and attribute results to controllable effort, strategy, and skill.
condition: when designing assessment backwash for self-management

statement: Judge the quality of a performance rather than the quality of the person who produced it.
condition: when applying criterion-referenced assessment

statement: Correct a grading inconsistency when two performances meet the same criterion level, even if discovering it required comparison between the scripts.
condition: when comparison reveals that a standard was applied inconsistently
exception: the revised grade must be justified by the criteria, not by forcing equal outcomes for unequal work

statement: Do not attach expected grade percentages to qualitative descriptors, because a quota overrides the stated performance standard whenever cohort attainment differs from expectation.
condition: when moving from marks or curves to criterion-referenced grading
exception: forecast distributions may be used diagnostically but must not determine individual grades

statement: Keep non-academic issues such as lateness, harassment, stress, or supervision failures out of the academic-quality grade and address them through separate procedures.
condition: when reporting what a piece of work demonstrates academically
exception: professional conduct may be graded when it is explicitly part of the intended outcome and criteria

statement: Assess functioning knowledge through an active performance resembling its real use rather than through verbal retelling alone.
condition: when the intended outcome requires application or professional action
exception: verbal or written explanation is appropriate when declarative knowledge is itself the outcome

statement: Use a varied assessment programme when different outcomes require individual, paired, group, reflective, portfolio, or examination evidence.
condition: when no single task authentically represents the outcome set
exception: each task should earn its place by providing distinct valid evidence rather than variety for its own sake

statement: Use contextualized practica, cases, and workplace tasks for functioning knowledge and reserve decontextualized writing or examinations primarily for declarative outcomes.
condition: when selecting an assessment context
exception: some outcomes validly combine contextualized performance with decontextualized explanation

statement: Do not assess only prerequisite declarative knowledge when the course outcome is the functioning knowledge built from it.
condition: when declarative content is a lead-in to application
exception: assess the prerequisite separately when its independent mastery is also required

statement: Use analytic component assessment formatively to diagnose strengths and weaknesses, then judge the final integrated performance holistically.
condition: when a task contains important distinguishable aspects but succeeds or fails as a whole
exception: a wholly analytic final decision is appropriate only when the intended outcome is explicitly a set of independent competencies

statement: Do not allow strength in one component to compensate for failure in a non-negotiable component essential to correct or safe whole performance.
condition: when component trade-offs could yield an unacceptable overall performance
exception: compensation is permissible among components whose trade-off is explicitly defensible in the standard

statement: Judge a whole performance in light of how its details combine to produce structure, impact, plausibility, or successful action rather than ignoring the details or merely adding them.
condition: when applying holistic assessment

statement: Accept assessor judgement as unavoidable and make its rationale examinable instead of disguising many small subjective decisions as an objective aggregate.
condition: when choosing between holistic judgement and numerical marking
exception: structured evidence and moderation should constrain judgement without pretending to remove it

statement: Equip assessors with a conceptual framework for relating parts to the whole; use a structure-of-learning model such as SOLO when it fits the outcome.
condition: when making holistic judgements about learning quality
exception: a discipline-specific framework may be more appropriate for some performances

statement: Use open-ended assessment tasks when outcomes include hypothesizing, creating, designing, or reflecting, so worthwhile responses need not match a predefined checklist.
condition: when intended performances are divergent
exception: essential constraints and standards should still be stated

statement: Provide a route for learners to demonstrate relevant, high-quality outcomes that were not predicted by a narrow question.
condition: when a rich learning context can produce valuable unintended learning consistent with course aims
exception: unexpected evidence must still satisfy the relevant outcome standard

statement: Use learner-generated questions, reflective journals, critical incidents, or portfolios to surface relevant learning that fixed examination questions may miss.
condition: when assessing open or unintended outcomes
exception: the selected evidence still needs verification and judgement against criteria

statement: Allow learners to use different evidence or tasks to meet the same outcome when comparison between learners is not the decision purpose.
condition: when criterion-referenced assessment can validate multiple authentic routes
exception: alternative evidence must be comparable in relevance, sufficiency, and standard

statement: Do not equate fairness with identical tasks when learner differences and multiple valid performances make equal access to the same standard more appropriate.
condition: when assessing originality, creativity, portfolios, or other individualized evidence
exception: identical conditions remain necessary for a decision explicitly based on relative comparison

statement: Treat assessment design as three separable decisions: defining criteria, selecting relevant evidence, and judging how well the evidence meets the criteria.
condition: when assigning roles in assessment

statement: Involve students, where appropriate, in discussing criteria, selecting evidence, and making self or peer judgements rather than reserving every assessment decision for the teacher.
condition: when participation advances the intended assessment literacy or professional judgement
exception: the institution may retain final authority for high-stakes certification

statement: Have learners apply criteria to their own and others' work so they gain first-hand understanding of what quality means and can reflect on shortcomings.
condition: when developing assessment literacy
exception: initial practice should be calibrated against exemplars or expert feedback

statement: Teach learners to select evidence that genuinely supports a criterion rather than merely telling them what evidence the teacher would choose.
condition: when portfolios, learning contracts, or professional decisions require evidence selection

statement: Use self- and peer judgement to prepare learners for professional decisions about their own performance, others' work, and the quality of abundant information.
condition: when professional or lifelong learning requires independent quality judgement
exception: high-stakes external consequences require suitable oversight and accountability

statement: Evaluate reliability in standards-based assessment through the consistency of the same judge over time and agreement among different judges on the same performance.
condition: when qualitative judgements determine achievement levels
exception: test-retest and internal-consistency statistics address different measurement-model questions

statement: Improve judgement reliability by spelling out grading standards in rubrics and calibrating assessors in the conceptual framework behind them.
condition: when multiple or repeated holistic judgements must be dependable
exception: rubrics cannot substitute for assessor understanding of the whole performance

statement: Ground dependable assessment in clarity about intended outcomes, admissible evidence, and the rationale for judging that evidence.
condition: when using a standards model

statement: Judge standards-based validity from whether the assessment's interpretations, uses, and learning consequences align with the intended outcomes and target performance domain.
condition: when validating an educational assessment
exception: external correlation evidence may supplement but does not replace alignment evidence

statement: Treat an assessment as invalidating its purpose when its predictable backwash induces rote model-answer learning that conflicts with the intended performance.
condition: when consequential test preparation changes how students learn
exception: memorization is not adverse when accurate recall is the intended outcome

statement: Allow a standards-based assessment to be multidimensional across the course outcomes and provide conditions that let individuals demonstrate optimal performance.
condition: when the course has multiple intended outcomes and the decision is individual attainment
exception: a single-outcome assessment may legitimately be unidimensional

statement: Audit assessment practice across purpose, student participation, openness, authenticity, reference model, criteria, quality judgement, and treatment of the whole to identify misalignment.
condition: when moving toward constructively aligned assessment

statement: Use pre-existing standards to award grades, and use comparisons only to check whether those standards were applied consistently.
condition: when a comparison between scripts reveals a possible halo effect or inconsistent judgement
exception: do not change the standard to preserve a desired rank order

statement: Design every assessment task to reveal how well the relevant outcome was achieved without steering learners toward memorization, question spotting, or other low-level shortcuts.
condition: when selecting an assessment task
exception: memorization may be relevant where exact recall is explicitly intended

statement: Explain grade criteria in a rubric that students understand before assessment and can use afterward to compare their performance with higher-quality levels.
condition: when rubrics are intended to guide preparation and reflection
exception: avoid language so prescriptive that it closes legitimate alternative performances

statement: Use a well-designed synoptic task to gather evidence for several outcomes and reduce assessment overload.
condition: when the outcomes can be enacted together in an integrated project, capstone, or other large performance
exception: do not combine outcomes whose evidence or standards cannot be distinguished sufficiently

statement: Use multiple tasks as complementary evidence for one outcome when each exposes a relevant aspect or context of achievement.
condition: when one performance sample is insufficient for a dependable outcome judgement
exception: additional tasks should not duplicate evidence without improving the decision

statement: Allocate student effort, assessor effort, and grade influence across assessment tasks in proportion to the educational importance of the outcomes they evidence.
condition: when planning an assessment programme
exception: minimum certification requirements may impose non-proportional constraints that should be made explicit

statement: Do not let a compulsory examination dominate the grade when it samples less-important declarative outcomes while more-important functioning outcomes receive little weight.
condition: when institutional rules prescribe a large examination percentage
exception: a dominant examination is defensible only if it validly represents the dominant intended outcomes

statement: Check that assessment workload and resource demands are manageable for both learners and staff before adopting an otherwise valid task.
condition: when scaling tasks such as portfolios or rich performance assessments
exception: manageability should prompt redesign, not automatic replacement with a misaligned task

statement: Treat each task result as evidence toward intended-outcome achievement rather than assuming the task score is itself the educational outcome.
condition: when an outcome is evidenced across one or more tasks
exception: a task and outcome may coincide when the task directly enacts the complete outcome

statement: Select assessment formats for their characteristic learning backwash as well as their logistical convenience.
condition: when choosing among examinations, assignments, essays, objective tests, or other formats

statement: Combine a breadth-oriented task with a depth-oriented assignment when one format cannot validly sample both coverage and deep understanding.
condition: when declarative outcomes require acquaintance across topics and sustained analysis of at least one topic
exception: the combined workload and weighting must remain proportionate

statement: Avoid routine multiple-choice assessment for higher-level outcomes unless items have been deliberately validated to elicit the required problem solving or reasoning.
condition: when outcomes require explaining, arguing, analysing, or comparing
exception: carefully constructed items in some mathematical and scientific domains can assess high-level reasoning

statement: Use extended prose when learners must construct an explanation, argument, analysis, or comparison that reveals the structure of their declarative understanding.
condition: when higher-level declarative outcomes are central
exception: writing demands should not contaminate the assessment of an unrelated outcome without support or accommodation

statement: Use timed invigilated examinations primarily when they validly sample breadth and accuracy or when secure conditions are necessary, not merely because they are administratively familiar.
condition: when deciding whether an examination belongs in the assessment programme
exception: institutional requirements may constrain the choice but do not establish educational validity

statement: Complement convergent examinations with assessment that lets students present relevant evidence or constructions the examiner did not anticipate.
condition: when course outcomes include open, divergent, or richly contextual learning
exception: closed assessment may suffice for narrowly specified breadth and accuracy outcomes

statement: Apply a time limit only when speed under pressure is part of the target performance; otherwise assess time-critical functioning knowledge in its authentic performance context.
condition: when deciding whether assessment should be timed
exception: a practical time boundary may still be needed for administration, but its validity impact must be considered

statement: If retaining an examination, design it to require an integrated view of the course rather than predictable fragments, so review can support consolidation instead of question spotting.
condition: when a timed examination assesses declarative understanding

statement: Anticipate that timed examinations will increase memorization; whether it becomes rote or structurally meaningful depends on the task demands and learners' approaches.
condition: when students prepare for timed recall and writing
exception: open-resource or authentic performance formats can reduce the premium on detail memorization

statement: Use open-book examinations to reduce detail memorization only after teaching students to organize and select resources efficiently under time constraints.
condition: when an exam should emphasize higher-level use of accessible information
exception: open access does not fix a task whose questions still reward shallow reproduction
